work: title: Itinerarium peregrinorum et gesta regis Ricardi
bibliography: note(s): Book 2 starts on fol. 18v, book 3 on fol. 29v, book 4 on 33v, book 5 on fol. 43v and book 6 on fol. 53v. ; The Itinerarium survives in twelve manuscripts, representing four different versions of the text. Scholars have established that the original version, consisting of only the first part of the first book, was written c. 1191-92 by an English crusader drawing on eyewitness accounts, particularly of the siege of Acre. The longer version of the text found in MS Ff.1.25(4) was written later, c. 1217-1220, and incorporates the original version and several other sources. The rubric in this manuscript attributes the Itinerarium to Geoffrey of Vinsauf, but this is a mistake probably caused by the copyist extracting details from the final rubric of Geoffrey's work which followed the chronicle in his exemplar. The actual author of the longer version has been identified as Ricardus de Templo, canon and prior of Holy Trinity Augustinian priory in London.

bibliography: note(s): Lessons for use at Matins on Thursday, Friday and Saturday in Holy Week, resembling those prescribed in the Tridentine Breviary. 208r-208v has two lessons from Lamentations, the first (Lam. 1:1-13) with a few neumes at the beginning and ending on 208v; the second (Lam.1:14 to 2:2) ending imperfect nec pepercit omnia. Folios 209-12 are missing. Folios 213r-214v has part of no. 7 followed by nos 8 and 9 of another series of lessons, with Augustine, Enarratio in Psalmum LXIII (CCSL xxxviii, 811-14). No. 7 contains paras 6-7, beg. Qui non opus habebat ...; no. 8 contains paras 8-9, beg. Repente sagittabunt ... ending 213v; 9 contains paras 10-12, beg. Narraverunt et absconderunt, ending 214v. Then follows Verbum in sabbato. Quomodo obscuratum est aurum ... Lam. 4: 1-7, 9-11 and a second lesson consisting of Lam. 4: 12-20 breaking off cui diximus in umbra tua the rest lost. F i, which has long served as the front endleaf, comes from the same art. and possibly once formed 210. It contains part of another series of lessons, beginning with the end of lesson 5 (1 Cor. 11: 33 to 12:3), beg. convenitis ad manducandum ...; 6 contains 1 Cor. 12: 4-20; 7 contains Augustine, Enarratio in Psalmum LXIII para. 2, ending on the verso; 8 contains para 3 ending qui venerat curare eos excogita[verunt]. 215-18 and the rest lost. Folio i recto-i verso, which may once have formed part of the same article, contains part of another series of lessons.

work: title: ‘IN NOMINE DOMINI INCIPIUNT OMELIE SIUE TRACTATUS BEATORUM AMBROSII AUGUSTINI HIERONIMI LEONIS MAXIMI GREGORII ET ALIORUM CATHOLICORUM PATRUM LEGENDAE.’ Followed by the prefatory verses ‘Summo apici rerum regi dominoque potenti’
Carolus Dei fretus auxilio ...; Cum diuina semper domi forisque clementia ... tradimus ad legendum.'
Cum appropinquassent Ierosolimis. Omelia beati Iohannis episcopi. Puto res ipsa exigit ut queramus. Hom. (Winter) 2.
Erunt signa in sole. Omelia beati Gregorii papae. Dominus ac redemptor noster paratos nos inuenire desiderans. Hom. 3.
Sermo beati Maximi episcopi de aduentu Domini. Igitur quando post tempus specialibus epulis reficere nos debemus. Hom. 4.
Cum audisset Iohannes in uinculis. Omelia beati Gregorii pape. Querendum nobis est f. k. Iohannes propheta et plus quam propheta. Hom. 5.
Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Superiore dominica capitulum euangelicum differentes partem quandam. Hom. 6.
Item sermo beati Augustini episcopi de aduentu Domini. Qui sunt in illa nocte duo in lecto. Hom. 7.
Miserunt Iudei. Omelia beati Gregorii pape. Ex huius nobis lectionis uerbis f. k. Iohannis humilitas commendatur. Hom. 8.
Sermo beati Augustini episcopi de unitate Trinitatis et de incarnatione Domini. Legimus sanctum Moysen populo Dei precepta dantem. Hom. 9.
Item sermo beati Augustini episcopi de incarnatione Domini. Vos inquam conuenio O Iudei qui usque in hodiernum negastis filium Dei. Hom. 10.
Missus est angelus. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Exordium nostrae redemptionis f. k. hodierna nobis sancti euangelii lectio commendat. Hom. 11.
Exurgens Maria in diebus illis. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Lectio sancti euangelii quam audiuimus et redemptionis nostrae. Hom. 12.
Anno quintodecimo imperii Tyberii. Omelia beati Gregorii pape. Redemptoris nostri precursor quo tempore uerbum predicationis acceperit. Hom. 13.
Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Laeticia quanta sit quantusque concursus. Hom. 14.
Cum esset desponsata. Omelia Origenis. Quae fuit necessitas ut desponsata esset Maria Ioseph. Hom. 15.

In sancta nocte. Primo tempore Alleuiata est terra Zabulon. Secunda. Consolamini consolamini populus meus. Tertia. Super montem excelsum ascende tu. Quarta Consurge consurge induere fortitudine tua Syon. Hom. 15 bis (a)-(c). In secundo nocturno. Saluator noster d. hodie natus est gaudeamus. Hom. 17. Sexta. Virgo regia Dauiticae stirpis eligitur. LEO, Tract. 21. Septima. Merito uirgineae integritatis nihil corruptionis intulit partus salutis. ibid. Octaua. Beati Ysidori. Natalis Domini dies ea de causa a patribus uotiuae sollempnitatis institutus est. Hom. 16.
Liber generationis. Mattheus suscepisse intellegitur incarnationem Domini ... quod gentis suae consuetudinem secutus sit.
Exiit edictum. Omelia beati Gregorii pape. Quia largiente Domino missarum sollempnia ter hodie celebraturi sumus. Hom. 24.
Pastores loquebantur adinuicem. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Nato in Betlehem Domino saluatore. Hom. 25.
In principio. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Quia temporalem mediatoris Dei et hominum hominis Iesu Christi. Hom. 26.
Sermo beati Augustini episcopi. Dominus noster Iesus Christus f. k. qui in aeternum est cunctae creator. AUGUSTINE, Serm. app. 128.
Sermo Leonis pape. Exultemus in Domino d. et spiritali iocunditate letemur. Hom. 18.
Sermo beati Fulgentii archiepiscopi de natiuitate Domini. Cupientes aliquid de huius diei sollempnitate narrare. Hom. 19.
Item de natiuitate Domini. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Iustissime f. festiuitate presentis diei in omne se gaudium totus ubique. Hom. 20.
Item cuius supra. Hodie f. k. Christus natus est nos renati. Hom. 21.
Item cuius supra. Sermo de natiuitate Domini. In aduentu dominico f. k. solutus est omnis paterne preuaricationis metus. Hom. 22.
Item ut supra sermo de natiuitate Domini. Hodierni misterii sacramentum f. k. sicut credidistis semper et creditis reparatio. Hom. 23.
Sermo beati Maximi episcopi de natiuitate Domini. Inuestigabiles humanis sensibus dispositiones esse diuinas ipsa operum. Hom. 23a.
Item sermo beati Maximi de natiuitate Domini. In aduentu dominico f. k. cui honorem debitum presenti festiuitate deferimus. Hom. 23b.
In natale sancti Stephani protomartyris. Heri celebrauimus temporalem sempiterni regis nostri natalem. Hom. 27.
Item in natale eiusdem beati Stephani protomartiris. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Lectio actuum apostolorum quae nobis hodie lecta est. Hom. 28.
Item sermo beati Augustini episcopi de miraculis eiusdem beati martiris Stephani. Ad aquas Tibilitanas episcopo referente proiecto martiris gloriosissimi Stephani memoriam. Hom. 29.
Dicebat Iesus turbis Iudeorum. Sermo ex commentario Ieronimi presbiteri. Hoc quod antea dixeram uos implete mensuram patrum uestrorum. Hom. 30.
Ex hystoria aecclesiastica relatio de beato Iohanne apostolo. Audi fabulam non fabulam sed rem gestam de Iohanne apostolo. Hom. 32.
Sermo beati Ysidori episcopi. Iohannes apostolus et euangelista filius Zebedei. Hom. 31.
Dixit Iesus Petro Sequere me. Venerabilis Bede presbiteri. Lectio sancti euangelii quae nobis lecta est f. mei tanto maiori. Hom. 33.
In natale innocentum. Sermo beati Seuerini episcopi. Zelus quo tendat quo prosiliat liuor. Hom. 34.
Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi de innocentibus. Dedicatur nouus ab infantibus sermo. Hom. 35.
Angelus Domini apparuit in somni Ioseph. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. De morte preciosa martyrum Christi innocentium sacra nobis est. Hom. 36.
Erat Ioseph et Maria mater Ihesu mirantes. Omelia Origenis. Congregemus in unum ea quae in ortu Ihesu dicta scriptaque sunt de eo. Hom. 41a.
In octaua Domini. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Quamquam non dubitem uos k. per paternam sollicitudinem instructione. Hom. 37.
Sermo Origenis de circumcisione Domini. Quod mortuus est Christus peccato mortuus est non quia ipse peccauerit. Hom. 38.
Sermo S. Ambrosii episcopi. Circumciditur itaque puer. Hom. 39.
Postquam consummati sunt dies octo. Omelia uenerabilis Bene presbiteri. Sanctam uenerandamque presentis festi memoriam paucis quidem. Hom. 40.

In epiphania Domini. Omnes sitientes (Is. 55: 1). Querite Dominum dum inueniri potest ... in pace deducemini. Haec. (Is. 55: 6-12). Surge illuminare Hierusalem ... maiestatismeae glorificabo. Haec (Is. 60: 1-7). Gaudens gaudebo ... ponat Iherusalem laudem in terra (Is. 61: 10-62: 7). Sermo Leonis in secundo nocturno. Celebrato proxime die quo intemerata uirginitas. Hom. 42.
Item sermo de epiphania. Gaudete in Domino d. iterum dico gaudete. Quoniam breui interuallo temporis post sollempnitatem natiuitatis Christi. Hom. 43.
Item cuius supra. Quamuis sciam d. quod sanctitatem uestram hodiernae festiuitatis causa non lateat. Hom. 44.
Item unde supra. In hac d. celebritate sicut relatu paternae traditionis instruimur. Hom. 45.
Cuius supra de eodem. Audistis f. lectionem euangelii salutaria presentis diei sacramenta recitantem. Hom. 46.
Unde supra. Sermo Fulgentii episcopi. Nostis k. f. quia dies iste qui nobis in honorem Domini per annos singulos celebratur. Hom. 47.
Cum natus esset Ihesus in Bethleem. Omelia beati Gregorii pape. Sicut ex lectione euangelica f. k. audistis caeli rege nato rex terrae turbatus est. Hom. 48.
Vidit Iohannes Ihesum uenientem. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae p. Iohannes baptista et precursor Domini Saluatoris quem diu uenturum populis predicauerat uerbo. Hom. 49.
Sermo beati Maximi e. Quamuis d. f. Christus salutis nostre Dominus omnipotentis Patris Filius coaeternus uelamine carnis. Hom. 50.
Item unde supra. Ait prophetarum precipuus Esyas sicut audistis k. illuminare illuminare Ierusalem. Hom. 51.
De eodem die. Salutare nobis est f. atque conueniens ut concurrentes ad festa dominica. Hom. 52.
Item cuius supra. Conplura nobis f. atque diuersa festiuitas presentis diei salutarium misteria. Hom. 53.
Item eiusdem de eodem die. Licet f. d. de sollempnitate diei huius ueterum sit diuersa traditio. Hom. 54.
Item eiusdem de eodem die. Redemptionis nostrae auctor aeternus omnipotens Deus unigenitus Dei uiui inseparabilis. Hom. 55.
Item de eodem epiphaniorum diae. Sermo beati Leonis papae. Iustum et rationabile d. uere pietatis obsequium est. Hom. 56.
Item de eodem die. Hodiernam festiuitatem d. apparitio Domini et Saluatoris nostri sicut nostis inlustrat. Hom. 57.

In octauas Teophaniae. Venit Ihesus a Galilea in Iordanem. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae p. Lectio sancti euangelii quam modo f. audiuimus magnum nobis et in domino et in seruo dat perfecte humilitatis exemplum. Hom. 58.
Cum esset Ihesus annorum duodecim. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Aperta est nobis f. k. euangelii lectio recitata. Hom. 59.
Nuptiae factae sunt in Chana. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae p. Quod Dominus noster atque Saluator ad nuptias uocatus. Hom. 60.
Cum autem descendisset Ihesus de monte. Omelia Origenis. Docente in monte Domino discipuli uenerunt ad eum sicut alacres. Hom. 61.
Ascendente Ihesu in nauiculam. Omelia Origenis. Ingrediente Domino in nauiculam secuti sunt eum discipuli eius. Hom. 64.
Respondens Iesus dixit Confiteor. Sanctum euangelium cum legeretur audiuimus exultasse Dominum. AUGUSTINE, Serm. 67.
In natiuitate sanctae Agnetis uirginis. Sermo beati Maximi e. Cum in toto mundo uirgineus flos Mariae inmarcescibiles coronas innectat. Hom. 62.
Item unde supra. Sermo beati Ambrosii episcopi. Inmaculatus Dominus inmaculatam sibi familiam. Hom. 63.
In purificatione sanctae Mariae uirginis. Sermo beati Augustini episcopi. Hodierna dies f. k. magnum nobis contulit gaudium ... peccatores saluos facere Ihesus Christus .... PL 95. 1461-3.
Item unde supra. Et ecce homo erat in Ierusalem. Non solum ab angelis et prophetis a parentibus et a pastoribus. Hom. 66.
Postquam impleti sunt dies purgationis eius. Omelia Augustini. Sollempnitatem nobis hodiernae celebritatis quam quadragesimo dominicae natiuitatis die. Hom. 67.
In septuagesima. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Dignitas humanae originis facile agnoscitur considerata sublimitate auctoris. Hom. 68.
Simile est regnum caelorum homini patri familias. Omelia beati Gregorii papae. In explanatione sua multa ad loquendum sancti euangelii lectio postulat. Hom. 69.
In lxa. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Nemo qui nesciat a principio hominem sic a Deo plasmatum. Hom. 70.
Sermo beati Iohannis e. De fide Abraham. Fides est religionis sanctissimae fundamentum caritatis uinculum. Hom. 72.
Assumpsit Ihesus duodecim discipulos suos. Omelia beati Gregorii papae. Redemptor noster preuidens ex passione sua. Hom. 73.
In xla. Sermo beati Leonis papae. Licet nobis d. appropinquauit festiuitate paschali ieiunium quadragesimae. Hom. 74.
Eodem die. Sermo beati Maximi. Ante dies deuotionem sanctae quadragesimae predicantes sacrarum litterarum exempla protulimus. Hom. 75.
Ductus est Ihesus in desertum. Omelia beati Gregorii papae. Dubitari a quibusdam solet a quo spiritu sit Ihesus ductus in desertum. Hom. 76.
De xla. Sermo Leonis. Semper quidem nobis d. sapienter et iuste uiuere decet. Hom. 77.
De xla. Predicaturus uobis d. sacratissimum maximumque ieiunium quo apertius utar exordio. Hom. 78.
Unde supra. Apostolica d. doctrina nos ammonet ut deponentes ueterem hominem cum actibus suis. Hom. 79.
Item de xla. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Audistis k. sicut euangelica tuba cecinit Dominum ac redemptorem nostrum aduersus temptamenta diaboli reluctantem. Hom. 80.
Omelia beati Maximi episcopi. Conflictus iste mirabilis quem inter caeli regem et regni caelestis tyrannum fuisse. Hom. 81.
Item cuius supra. Aduertite f. k. quanta nobis spiritalis uitae documenta succrescunt. Hom. 82.
Item unde supra. Quia non nullorum est consuetudo k. aduenientes quadragesimae dies deuotiore ieiunio preuenire. Hom. 84.
Sermo Iohannis e. de Iacob et Esau. Portabat Rebecca geminos in utero fratres ante ortus principia bellatores. Hom. 85.
Ihesus secessit in partes Tyri. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. In lectione sancti euangelii quae modo nobis lecta est f. k. audiuimus magnam mulieris fidem. BEDE, Hom. I, 22.
Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Mittitur a Iacob patre sanctissimo Ioseph sanctus ad fratres. Hom. 88.
De confessione peccati. Sermo Iohannis episcopi. Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus est. Spiritus Sanctus medelam purgandi facinoris et curam admissi delicti obtulit. Hom. 89.
Erat Ihesus eiciens daemonium. Omelia ex conmentario uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Daemoniacus iste apud Matheum non solum mutus sed et cecus fuisse narratur. Hom. 90.
Extollens uocem. Omelia ex commentario uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Magne deuotionis et fidei haec mulier ostenditur ... sed negare et blasphemare quaerebant. In Luc. 4; PL 92. 479-80.
Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Stabat Moyses in monte non armis sed precibus pugnaturus. Hom. 91.
Abiit Ihesus trans mare Galileae. Omelia beati [Bede presbiteri added s. xv]. Qui signa et miracula Domini ad Saluatoris recte cum legunt. Hom. 92.
Dominica in passione Domini. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Magnum Hieremie sanctissimi meritum magnum in eum conlatum est diuinitus donum. Hom. 93.
Quis ex uobis arguet me de peccato. Omelia beati Gregorii papae. Pensate f. k. mansuetudinem Dei. Hom. 94.
In tradicione symboli. Sermo Maximi. Cum aput patres nostros sicut liber Iudicum refert. Hom. 95.
Sermo beati Maximi. Psalme uicesimi primi qui lectus est seriem decursiri diligenter prius debemus intendere. Hom. 96.
Dominica in palmis. Cum appropinquassent Hierosolimis. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Mediator Dei et hominum homo Christus Ihesus. Hom. 97.
Feria secunda. Sermo Leonis. Desiderata nobis d. et uniuerso optabilis mundo adest festiuitas. Hom. 98.
Proximum erat pascha Iudeorum. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Moris esse prudentium solet non solum ex eis quae recte apprehenderint. Hom. 99.
Feria tertia. Sermo Leonis. Gloria d. dominicae passionis de qua nos etiam hodie locuturus esse promisimus. Hom. 100.
Item cuius supra. Sermonem d. de gloriosa Domini nostri Ihesu Christi passione promissum. Hom. 101.
Feria quarta. Sermo beati Leonis. Sacramentum d. dominicae passionis in salutem humani generis ante tempora aeterna dispositum. Hom. 102.
Item cuius supra. Cum multis modis d. Iudaica impietas laboraret ut causam aliquam perpetrandi. Hom. 103.

In cena Domini. Quomodo sedet sola ciuitas ... ne intrarent in aecclesiam tuam Ierusalem (Lam. 1: 1-10), neumed. In secundo nocturno. Exaudi orationem meam cum tribulor. Seuierunt inimici in martyres. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63. 2-3 (CCSL 39, pp. 808 line 28 ‑ 809 line 11).
Ante diem festum Paschae. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae p. Scripturus euangelista Iohannes memorabile illud Domini ministerium. Hom. 105.
Sermo Leonis. Scio quidem d. paschale festum tam sublimis esse mysterium. Hom. 104.

De excelso misit Dominus ignem in ossibus meis ... et cor meum merens Ierusalem (Lam. 1: 13-), neumed. Protexisti me a conuentu malignantium. Iam ipsum caput nostrum intueamur. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63.
In Parasceue. Decursis d. sermone proximo his quae ad comprehensionem Domini precesserunt. Hom. 106.
Sermo de cruce et latrone ad collationem legendus. Hodie incipiamus k. de crucis tropheo predicare et honoremus hanc diem magis.

In sabbato sancto. Dissipauit Dominus quasi ortum tentorium suum ... gaudium uniuersae terrae Ierusalem (Lam. 2: 6-15), neumed. Sagittae infantium factae sunt plage eorum. Quo perduxerunt illas scrutationes suas quas perscrutantes defecerunt ... (ends impf.) ab origine mundi. Nunc autem. AUGUSTINE, Enarr. in Ps. 63.

Originally blank, is an addition little later than the main book (Pl. 63b): 'Nouerint omnes Christi fedeles tam futuri quam presentes quod ego F. Dei gratia Romanorum imperator rogatu fundatorum nouae cellae Sancti Iohannis Baptistae in Holz rogatu etiam ancillarum Dei inibi consistentium regali clementia locum ipsum in nostram tuitione susceperimus ...'. pr. James, Peterhouse, pp. 157-8; pr., from late copies, in MGH Diplomata 10/4 (1990), no. 1078, where it is described as a forgery. On f. 180bv, in a rough hand of s. xiii or xiv, a metrical computus: 'Celestem benedicimus artificem Galilei ... Intelligis istum compotum sic: Que sunt litere in uerbo tot sunt septimano a proxima dominica post natalem Domini usque ad dominicam Inuocauit me. Et super qualibet litera prima in uerbo erit litera dominicalis et in inceptione cuiuslibet uersus erit bisextus et semper recurrit.'
In natale apostolorum Philippi et Iacobi. Non turbetur cor uestrum. Omelia beati Augustini episcopi. Erigenda est nobis f. ad Deum maior intentio. Hom. (Summer) 23. 112.
Sermo in translatione sancti Benedicti abbatis. Festiua beatissimi Benedicti sollempnitas Christo Domino propiciante refulget. ODO OF CLUNY 3; PL 133. 721-9.

Incipit prologus de sancta Maria Magdalena. Liquet plerisque relationis series prolixioris materiae stilo mandata qualiter beata Maria Magdalena diuina ordinante clementia ...; Incipit de transitu sanctae Mariae Magdalenae. Post dominicae igitur resurrectionis gloriam ... corporis reportat beneficia cui omnis honor et gloria .... Nunc ergo largiente Domino aggrediamur exponere qualiter gleba corporis eiusdem sacratissime Mariae Magdalenae ...; Post aliqua uero temporum curricula deficiente regum
Rogabat quidam phariseus. Cogitanti michi de Mariae penitentia flere magis libet quam aliquid dicere. GREGORY, Hom. in Evang. 33.
Liber generationis. Omelia lectionis eiusdem. In huius sancti euangelii exordio beatus Matheus ostendit generationem ... facit perenni nomine Christianos. RABANUS, In Matt. 1 (PL 107. 731-8).
In exaltatione sanctae crucis. Tempore illo postquam Constantino Augusto properanti contra Maxentium tyrannum. BHL 4178.
Eodem die passio sancti Cypriani Cartaginensis episcopi et martyris. Valeriano tercio et Galieno secundo consulibus Cartagine in secretario. BHL 2037.
Sermo beati Augustini in natale sancti Cypriani episcopi et martyris. Sancta sollempnitas beatissimi martyris Cypriani quae nos in nomine Domini congregauit. AUGUSTINE, Serm. ined. 14; PL 46. 862-6.
Item unde supra de uersu Psalmi. Psalmum cantauimus Benedictus Deus qui non dedit nos in uenationem dentibus eorum ... filii sunt insultantium. id., 15; PL 46. 866-9.
Sermo Maximi episcopi de eadem festiuitate. Sancti Cypriani festiuitatem sicut omnibus notum est hodie celebramus. Hom. 78.
Sermo cuius supra de eodem sancto martyre. In martyrio beatissimi Cypriani f. k. uniuersa nobiscum Christi aecclesia exultat. Hom. 79.
Sermo sancti Ambrosii episcopi de uirginibus. Cum in toto mundo uirgineus flos Mariae inmarcescibiles coronas innectat. No. 66 again.

Passio sanctorum martyrum Saturi, Saturnini fratrum, Reuocati et Felicitatis sororis eius et Perpetuae. [F]acta itaque persecutione sub Valeriano et Gallieno comprehensi sunt uenerabiles uiri iuuenes ... atque participes eorum efficere dignetur in gloriam et laudem nominis sui quod est benedictum in s. s. amen. Explicit passio sanctorum martyrum. BHL 6634. On f. 211v, added s. xiii (Pl. 63c), 'Notum sit omnibus in Christo fidelibus tam futuris [then in another hand Ich beswer hiute dine hir bidem hailigen Christe der sich zemarterunne durch alle man kuenn per sanctam Mariam matrem Domini ... dru wihe min frawe sancte Marie amen.]' A prayer for protection from eye disease, often edited, e.g. F. Wilhelm, Denkmäler deutscher Prosa des 11. und 12. Jahrhunderts (2 vols., Munich, 1914, 1916, repr. in one vol. Munich, 1960), 1. 52-3, 2. 134-5; the dialect is Bavarian. At the foot is written 'Nagel'.
Fuit in diebus Herodis. Omelia uenerabilis Bede prespiteri. Venturus in carne Dominus et redemptor noster. Hom. 40.
In natale Iohannis Baptistae. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Sollemnitatem nobis diuersorum martyrum f. k. uitae presentis occasus. Hom. 41.
Item sermo unde supra. Cunctorum quidem prophetarum f. k. ueneranda recordatio est. Hom. 42.
Festiuitatem presentis diei f. k. uenerandi Iohannis Baptistae genuina natiuitas consecrauit. Hom. 43.
Hodie sancti Iohannis natalem f. k. celaebramus quod nulli unquam sanctorum legimus fuisse concessum. AUGUSTINE, Serm. 197.
Elisabeth impletum est tempus pariendi. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Precursoris Domini natiuitas sicut sacratissima lectionis euangelicae prodit hystoria. Hom. 44.

In uigilia apostolorum Petri Pauli. Dixit Ihesus Petro Symon Iohannis diligis me. Omelia uenerabilis Bede presbiteri. Virtutem nobis perfecte dilectionis presens sancti euangelii lectio commendat. Hom. 45.
In natale apostolorum Petri et Pauli Leonis papae. Omnium quidem sanctorum sollempnitatum d. totus mundus est particeps. Hom. 46.
Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Gloriosissimos Christianae fidei principes annuis sollempnitatibus honoramus. Hom. 47.
Venit Ihesus in partes Cesaraee Philippi. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Lectio sancti euangelii quam modo f. audistis tanto intentius cogitanda. Hom. 52.
Alius sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Apostolici natalis gaudio f. k. Petri et Pauli quorum hodie beatissimis passionibus iocundamur. Hom. 48.
Alius sermo cuius supra. Beatissimorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli inseperabilem fidem passionemque germanam omni nos deuotione f. necesse est celebrare. Hom. 49.
Item alius cuius supra. Beatissimorum apostolorum passio f. quorum hodie natalem sollempniter celebramus. Hom. 50.
Alius sermo Maximi episcopi. Cum omnes beati apostoli parem gratiam apud Dominum sanctitatis obtineant. Hom. 51.
De sancto Paulo apostolo. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Beatus Paulus qui tantam uim humanae alacritatis ostendit. Hom. 53.
Sermo Augustini e. Hodie lectio de actibus apostolorum haec pronuntiata est. Hom. Rom. 58.
Ecce nos reliquimus omnia. Omelia beati Iheronimi presbiteri. Grandis fiducia Petrus piscator erat. Hom. 54.
Amen dico uobis quod uos qui secuti estis me in regeneratione. Hic discimus cum suis discipulis indicaturum Ihesum. Hom. 55.
Iussit Iesus discipulos suos. Euangelium quod recentissime recitatum est de Domino Ihesu Christo. AUGUSTINE, Serm. 76.
Iussit Iesus discipulos suos. Cum sanctum euangelium legeretur audiuimus nauiculam periclitantem. Ps.-AUGUSTINE 72.
De sancta Maria Magdalena. Narrat Iosephus quod Maria Magdalena post ascensionem Domini et Saluatoris ... meritis eiusdem mulieris prestante Dominus noster I. C. cui .... BHL 5453b.
Accessit ad Iesum mater filiorum Zebedei. Dominus conditor et redemptor noster uulnera superbiae nostrae sanare desiderans. BEDE, Hom. II, 21.
In natale sancti Laurentii. Sermo Maximi episcopi. Sanctum est f. ac Deo placitum ut natalem beati Laurentii precipua deuotione ueneremur. Hom. 65.
Alius cuius supra. Sicut patrum nostrorum f. k. non incerta relatione didicimus. Hom. 66.
Item alius cuius supra. Beatissimi Laurentii f. k. annua semper noua festiuitas aecclesiam Dei iugiter in gaudia leticiae spiritualis accendit. Hom. 67.

Amen amen dico uobis nisi granum frumenti. Saluator noster d. discipulorum animos exhortans ad passionis suae sectando uestigia sumit exemplum de grano frumenti ... quae fidelibus sunt preparata peruenire mereamur per .... Homiliary of Mondsee, no. 107: H. Barré, Les homèliaires Carolingiens de l'école d'Auxerre (Studi e Testi 25 [1962], p. 243.
Sermo beati Ambrosii episcopi de assumptione sanctae Mariae uirginis. Celebritas hodierni diei ammonet ut in laude uirginis immorari debeamus. Ps.-ILDEFONSUS, Serm. 7.
Intrauit Iesus in quoddam castellum. Omelia beati Augustini episcopi. Verba Domini nostri I. C. quae modo ex euangelio recitata sunt ammonent nos esse unum. AUGUSTINE, Serm. 103.
Item unde supra. Hic theokos [sic] sacrae uersatur sermo Mariae (8 lines; SK 6764).
Sermo beati Iheronimi presbiteri de assumptione sanctae Mariae uirginis. Cogitis me O Paula et Eustochium immo karitas Christi compellit. Ps.-JEROME (PASCHASIUS), Epist. app. 9.
Intrauit. Omelia beati Augustini episcopi. Sanctum euangelium cum legeretur audiuimus a femina religiosa. Hom. Wolfenbüttel 76.
Unde supra. Sermo Beati [sic]. Intrauit. Adest nobis d. f. dies ualde uenerabilis dies omnium sanctorum sollempnitates precellens. Ps.-AUGUSTINE 208.
Inter precipuas sanctorum festiuitates k. hodierna nobis refulsit insignis gloriosae genitricis Dei Mariae. Ps.-ILDEFONSUS 2; PL 96. 250-4.
Omelia Anshelmi Cantuariensis ep. In scriptura sacra res una et eiusdem locutionis inuenitur diuersa significare. RALPH D'ESCURES; PL 95. 1505-6.

De epistola. Cum autem lectio de laude sapientie in eius die legatur causa satis probabili declaratur ... ut nos mortificatos uiciis participes faceret suae diuinitatis. HONORIUS AUGUSTODUNENSIS, Sigillum beatae Mariae (PL 172. 498-9).
Facta est contentio. Sicut bonis esse moris solet esse in Scripturis ... potestatis excrescant. PL 94. 423-5.
In decollatione sancti Iohannis Babtiste. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Hodie nobis Iohannis uirtus Herodis feritas cum refertur. Hom. 71.
Unde supra. Sermo beati Iohannis episcopi. Heu me quid agam? Unde sermonis exordium faciam? Hom. 72.
Audiuit Herodes tetrarcha fama Ihesu. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Natalem f. k. beati Iohannis diem celebrantes. Hom. 73.
In natiuitate sanctae Mariae uirginis. Liber generationis Ihesu Christi. Cum omelia require in maiori omelia in natiuitate Domini.
De Sancto Cypriano martyre. Sermo beati Maximi episcopi. Sancti Cypriani festiuitatem sicut omnibus notum est hodie celebramus. Hom. 78.

Dixit Dominus Iesus turbis Iudeorum Ego si exaltatus fuero. Que omnia nobis pandit sancti euangelii lectio recitata nisi a quibus princeps huius mundi eicitur foras? ... credite in ueritatem ut renascimini ex ueritate. AUGUSTINE, In Ioh., Tract. 52. 11-13, the beginning slightly altered.
Vidit Ihesu hominem sedentem. Omelia uenerabilis Bedae presbiteri. Legimus apostolo dicente quia omnes peccauerunt ... (ending impf.) ac pietatis gratiam prouocat nam. Hom. 99.

bibliography: note(s): Two leaves (f. i and pp. 489-490), one at each end of the earlier medieval textblock. Both leaves are former pastedowns, and have since been lifted. The leaves bear traces of adhesive residue and have been trimmed for reuse as binding waste, and as such, the text is illegible in some places and incomplete in others. Legal document written in a 16th century hand. The legal text is only present on one side of each leaf, i.e., f. i recto, and p. 490. The text refers to places in and around Cambridge including a 'Thomas Hobbeson in ecclesia parochiali sancti Clementis Cantabrigi' (Thomas Hobbeson in the ecclesiastical parish of St Clement's Cambridge); St Clement's church is on Bridge Street in Cambridge. This part of the document may contain a reference to the Thomas Hobson (c. 1544-1630) Hobson, Thomas, approximately 1544-1630 , citizen of Cambridge, haulier, stablemaster, and businessman. One difficulty with associating this note with him is that he moved to Cambridge in 1568 and lived on Trumpington Street, making him a parishoner of St Bene't's, where he is also buried. Other names visible in the document are 'Robert Stewkyn', and 'magistri Edwardi Heynes Notarii publicii'. There is also a reference to the village of Fenstanton.

bibliography: note(s): Two leaves (f. i and pp. 489-490), one at each end of the earlier medieval textblock. Both leaves are former pastedowns, and have since been lifted. The leaves bear traces of adhesive residue and have been trimmed for reuse as binding waste, and as such, the text is illegible in some places and incomplete in others. Legal document written in a 16th century hand. The legal text is only present on one side of each leaf, i.e., f. i recto, and p. 490. The text refers to places in and around Cambridge including a 'Thomas Hobbeson in ecclesia parochiali sancti Clementis Cantabrigi' (Thomas Hobbeson in the ecclesiastical parish of St Clement's Cambridge); St Clement's church is on Bridge Street in Cambridge. This part of the document may contain a reference to the Thomas Hobson (c. 1544-1630) Hobson, Thomas, approximately 1544-1630 , citizen of Cambridge, haulier, stablemaster, and businessman. One difficulty with associating this note with him is that he moved to Cambridge in 1568 and lived on Trumpington Street, making him a parishoner of St Bene't's, where he is also buried. Other names visible in the document are 'Robert Stewkyn', and 'magistri Edwardi Heynes Notarii publicii'. There is also a reference to the village of Fenstanton.

bibliography: note(s): NB: William Worcestre has inserted six documents into this manuscript that were created as separate textual units by other scribes and has added texts that are part of the Itineraria to them. This catalogue record treats these documents as separate parts. Parts 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 should be consulted for further items of the Itineraria. This catalogue record follows the edition of Harvey (1969) and considers a few items in Worcestre's hand as separate from the Itineraria. Page 333 is a torn leaf with a fragmentary text that has not been read (no text is visible on the reverse of this leaf or p. 334). Aside from historical and topographical information, the Itineraria include a wide range of other materials that evidently were of interest to Worcestre. For example, it includes a multiplication table that is attributed to Thomas Hengham, monk of Norwich Priory (Multiplicacio numerorum secundum laborem dompni Thome Hengham religiosi monasterij Norwicensis), on p. 261 [perhaps Thomas Ingham, monk scholar of Norwich, who was at Cambridge in 1466-67; see Harvey (1969), p. 239 fn. 1]; a list of Arabic terms for parts of the Astrolabe (Termeni arabici in jnstrumento astrolabij) on p. 261]; and notes on the art of grammar (Priscianus in Maiori) on p. 320.

work: title: Letter of R. Botoner to William Worcestre
paratext: explicit: 42 Sir youre blissyng and my modirs desirid I sent yow a letter by Master Paston man. Which is in that contre etcaetera. Sir I am with my maister Lovel God geue me grace to plese hym. And sir he wol nedis haue a bed and I haue take youre bed except feither-bed and bolster etcaetera. Sir your hostes made suche wark that I am not fare with her they wold nat let me haue the bed tyll my coson sent his man 39 No more etcaetera but God prospere you I pray yow comaund me to my modir and sister and brodir and all my frendis I pray yow remembre my mater I here no word of the ansuere of W.B. deuandes etcaetera youre boke is to Wynchestre etcaetera. Wrete on Tuesday iijd weke of Lent - R. Botoner
paratext: final rubric(s): 41 To William Worcestre this be delyuered / In hast etcaetera / loth to offend
bibliography: note(s): Dallaway (1834) identifies the writer as Worcestre's son Richard. The letter, which mentions Thomas Kent and a letter from a male member of the Paston family, is undated but may have been written between c 1460-c. 1480. Afther the death of John Fastolf in 1459, Worcestre, Fastolf's former secretary, became much involved with John Paston, one of Fastolf's executors, concerning the distribution of his possessions.; Written across p. 39 are the numbers 1448 [deleted: 1449]; and 1330 [deleted: 1330] in different ink.

bibliography: note(s): Willelmus de Beluero may be William de Belvero [of Belvoir], monk of St Albans, who became prior of Belvoir, Lincolnshire, in 1333 (on him, see 'Houses of Benedictine monks: The priory of Belvoir', in A History of the County of Lincoln: Volume 2, ed. William Page (London, 1906) at British History Online [accessed 11 November 2024]); but he may also be the Johannis de Belvero dudum canonici ecclesie Lincolniensis who died in 1391 and was buried in Lincoln Cathedral (for his brass inscription, see 'Lincoln Cathedral: A List of the Brasses Existing in 1641 ; from Mr. Peck's Collation of Bp. The document names Robertus de Swaffham; Alanus de Hemmyngston; Willelmus de Dynyeton (monk of Ely); Magister Geoffrey de ffreysyngfeld; Thomas de Helyesdon; Johannes de Leyham (chaplain); Willelmus Alston; Robertus de Pysale; Johannes de Melton; and John de Huntyngdon. bibliography: note(s): Fragment of a legal document, now cut down from its original size and probably used as a pastedown in a former binding. Partial notarial mark (notary signature) present in the upper outer corner of the leaf. The notarial mark is incomplete but appears to be the mark of John Stoberd, who acted as notary for Richard Fox Fox, Richard, 1447 or 1448-1528 (b. 1447 or 1448, d. 1528), founder of Corpus Christi College, Oxford and at various times Bishop of Exeter, Bath and Wells, Durham, and Winchester. John Stoberd acted as notary for Fox, when Fox admitted Thomas Cisson as Master of Baliol College, Oxford in 1511. The document admitting Cisson to the position of Master of Bailiol is now Oxford, Balliol College, Archives, MS D.3.3 and Stoberd's notarial mark can be seen in the lower portion of the document. The text is badly damaged but mentions an Abbot Richard in connection with the location Chale: this may refer to Richard Kennock who was rector of the parish church of Chale in the Isle of Wight c. 1516.

paratext: incipit: 6v Ly Reys Athewlter regna .xviij. aunz
paratext: explicit: 7r Puis Edward soun fuiz qe auoit Regne quant ceste date fu fete xviij aunz
bibliography: note(s): 'Athewlter' probably refers to King Aethelwulf - King Aethelwulf of Wessex reigned for 18 years and was followed by an Aethelbald (or 'Athelbaud' as he is described in this manuscript). Smallwood, in his discussion of the The Prophecies of the Six Kings to Follow John offered a general description of the Anglo-Norman texts on ff. 3v-10v and suggested that this regnal list must have been copied c. 1325/26, i.e., in the 18th regnal year of the reign of Edward II. Edward II is the final king in the regnal list, and in the list, Edward is said to have reigned for 18 years. King Edward II reigned for 20 years (1307-1327), but a scribe writing in the reign of Edward II would have only been able to state the duration of Edward's reign at the time of writing, e.g., 18 years which places the date of the composition of the regnal list c. 1325/1326.

work: title: Amuletic charm incorporating the Letter of Jesus to King Abgar
paratext: incipit: 9v Seynt leon apostoile de Rome escrit ceste lettre e dit ky vnkys le lirra ia cel iour ne estout detur sun enimi
paratext: explicit: 10r in dei nomine securus ambulabit
paratext: final rubric(s): 10r Explicit epistola quam dominum nostrum Ihesum Christum manum scriptam misit ad abagarem Regem qui eum videre desiderabit + Ihesus + Nazarenus + Rex + Iudeorum + Miserere mei +
bibliography: note(s): The opening lines of the text in this manuscript attribute it to a Pope Saint Leo ('Seynt leon apostoile de Rome', but as five Popes with the papal name Leo have been canonised (I, II, III, IV, and IX), it is unclear which Pope Leo is meant in the text). The closing lines of the text however, describe the text as a copy of the letter of Jesus to King Abgar of Edessa. The text is usually descibed in modern scholarship as an apocryphal letter of Jesus to King Abgar. The text suggests that people suffering from illnesses 'si homme seyt malade' should wear the letter around their neck 'pendet set bref autour sonn cole' in order to achieve relief from their symptoms. The text contains a formula of address, where a person performing the charm asks for help on behalf of another person, and in this letter, the intended recipient of the benefit of the charm is named in the text as 'William', 'assistunt hinc famulo tuo +Willelmo+ hoc scriptum portanti'; no further information is known about the identity of this William.

bibliography: note(s): The grant is undated. It is possible that the 'Walter de Emirus' mentioned in the text may be the former prior of the Hospitallers in Kilmainham, Dublin, better known as Walter de Aqua / Walter Dewyas / Walter de Ewyas. The Registrum de Kilmainham (now Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Rawlinson B 501 ) contains a copy of a grant on ff. 61rv of a 'Frater Walterus de Ewyas' who seems to have been Grand Prior of the hospitallers in Ireland for an unknown duration during the first quarter of the 14th century. The grant in MS Rawlinson B 501 has a witness list which includes some of the same people who witnessed the grant in CCCC MS 405 including 'fratre Laurencio ... fratre Dauid de Castello ... fratre Waltero de Lindeseya, fratre Rogero clerico, fratre Ada de Suandime ...'. The land referred to in the grant, 'Dromconan', probably refers to Drom Conáin / Drumcannon in County Waterford, Ireland.

bibliography: note(s): The Articuli Cleri were enacted on the 24th November 1316, in the reign of King Edward II. The date given here in the CCCC MS 412 copy of the Articuli Cleri is 23 November 1316. The Articuli Cleri were copied by Edmund Poplay who was Principal of Beef Hall in Oxford, c. 1496-1497; see Provenance for further information on Poplay. Poplay also wrote a note under the Articuli Cleri in which he included biographical information: 'Litera domini regis iusticiariis directa supra ponitur infra constituciones prouinciales de foro competenti C circumspecte agatis in quo C continentur omnes casus in quibus iudex ecclesiasticus cognoscere potest regia prohibitione non obstante . Melius tamen est quod non faciat nisi regiam consultacionem optineat etc. Edmundus poplay. Supplicat venerabili etc. Edmundus poplay in jure canonico Baccallarius quatenus studia quindecim annorum que habuit in hac uniuersitate in facultate arcium et in juribus Ciuili et canonico sibi sufficiant ad hunc effectum ut admittatur ad incipiendum in jure canonico ita quod soluat markam . Hec gracia concessa et confirmata est anno domini millesimo cccco lxxxxix mensia Jun. xiimo condicio talis est quod soluat uniuersitati xls'. The note is written in two different inks, the first ink a visual match for the rest of the Articuli Cleri, and the second ink, which begins at 'Supplicat venerabili etc ...' is darker and more opaque than the ink used for the writing in the rest of this Part.

work: title: Suffrage to St Thomas the Apostle
paratext: incipit: 2r [O] Thomas didime per Christum quem meruisti tangere te precibus rogamus altissonis sucurre nobis miseris ne dampnemur cum impijs in aduentu iudicis
paratext: explicit: 2r Da nobis quesumus domine beati apostoli tui thome sollempnitatibus gloriari ut eius semper et patrociniis subleveamur et fidem congrua deuotionis fectemur. Per Christum dominum nostrum
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 2v O eustachij genere nobilis quem probauit fortuna labilis
paratext: explicit: 2v Deus qui eustachium gloriosum martirem tuum in tentacionibus probasti et probatum coronasti ipsius sociorum que eius meritis et precibus in omni tribulatione tuum nobis presta auxilium et sempiterne consolationis interminabile gaudium Per dominum nostrum etcaetera
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.
St Cuthbert (Cuthberti) has been added to the Calendar (f. 7r) in a (?) 16th- or 17th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 9r Stirps regalis que vita floruit prolem profer regem quem docuit . Patrum pater patronum genuit Ninianum mundus quo claruit
paratext: explicit: 9r [D]eus qui populos pictorum et britonum per doctrinam sancti niniani episcopi et confessoris tui ad noticiam fidei conuertisti concede propicius vt cuius erudicione veritatis tue lucius perfundimur eius intercessione celestis patriam vite gaudia consequamur . Per Christum dominum etcaetera
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 10r O Jhesu Christe eterna dulcedo te amancium iubilus excedens omne gaudium et omne desiderium salus et amator peccatorum vere penitentium qui delicias tuas testatus es esse cum filijs hominum
paratext: explicit: 15r Ita laudabilis et post huius uite terminum te merear laudare cum omnibus sanctis tuis ineternum . Amen . Pater noster .
paratext: rubric(s): 10r Incipiunt quindecim orationes ad Christum

paratext: incipit: 15r [T]anto tempore vobiscum sum et non cognouistis me philippe philippe qui vidit me vidit et patrem meum . Gauuisi sunt discipuli domini . Viso domino
paratext: explicit: 15r [D]eus qui nos anima appostolorum tuorum philippi et iacobi solempnitate letificas presta quesumus vt quorum gaudemus meritis instruamur exemplis Per Christum dominum nostrum Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 16r Domine deus omnipotens pater et filius et spiritus sanctus N. uictoriam contra omnes inimicos nostros ut non resistere michi possuit nocere nec contra dicere sed dignatur uirtus eorum et consilium in bonum
paratext: explicit: 16v Christus in se confidentes saluat . Christus vincit . Christus regnat . Christus imperat . sic Christus imperare dignetur me esse triumphatorem omnium aduersariorum meorum ut non timebo quid faciat michi homo . psalmus . Deus in nomine tue saluum me . etcaetera . Deus misereatur nostri et benedicat . Kyrieleyson . Christeleyson . Christeleyson . Domine exaudi . Et clamor Oremus.
paratext: rubric(s): 16r Memoria de sancte trinitate
bibliography: note(s): This prayer is joint with the next prayer.

paratext: incipit: 16v Libera me domine ihesu Christe fili dei vnu qui in cruce suspensus fuisti et lancea perforari latus tuum permisisti et de precioso sanguine tuo redemisti
paratext: explicit: 17r Exaudi me domine sicut exaudisti mariam magdalenam peccatricem et dimissa sunt ei peccata multa quoniam dilexit multum libera me domine N. famulum tuum ab omni malo presenti preterito et futuro et exaudi . me domine in omnibus peticionibus meis et de necessitatibus meis et periculis meis libera me domine qui cum patre et spiritu sancto vnus et regnas deus per omnia secula seculorum . Amen. De profundis clamaui ad te domine utsupra.
bibliography: note(s): This prayer is joint with the previous prayer.

work: title: Suffrage to St John the Baptist
paratext: incipit: 18r Gaude iohannes baptista . qui in ventris clausus cista . Congaudebas domino .
paratext: explicit: 18v Beata iohannes baptiste Christi precursor atque preco redemptoris nostri porrige nobis manum misericordie tue et auxiliare nobis in omnibus necessitatibus nostris et angustijs et esto iugiter pius intercessor apud altissimi iudicis clementiam quatinus tuis meritis nos liberate dignetur ab omni tribulatione et augustia periculo et peccatorum tenebris eripiat et ad lucem celestis gaudij peducat Per Christum dominum nostrum . Amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 18r Memoria de sancto iohanne baptista

paratext: incipit: 19r [B]artholomeus celi cidus aureum milies supra solis iubar radians erige merites nostras polo turbidas egras que et nostras sana confidencias In omnem terram etcaetera
paratext: explicit: 19r [O]mnipotens sempiterne deus qui huius dieei veneranda sanctam que leticiam in beati bartholomee apostoli tui festiuitate tribuisti da ecclesie tue quesumus et amare quod credidit et predicare quod docuit Per Christum dominum nostrum Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 20r Gaude lux londoniarum thoma tutor animarum dei prouidentia . Natus matris matris die . sequens uitam uere me speciali gratia
paratext: explicit: 20v Deus qui beatum thomam martirem tuum atque pontificem die martis pro ecclesia tua uarijs tribulationibus oppressum gloria et honore coronasti fac nos quesumus suis meritis et precibus sic huius uite seculi miserias transire et ad celi gaudia possimus peruenire Per Christum dominum nostrum . Amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 20r Memoria de sancto thome cantuariensis

paratext: incipit: 20v-21r [B]eati eritis cum vos oderunt homines et cum seperauerint vos et exprobrauerunt et eiecerint nomine vestrum tanquam malum propter filium homines gaudete exultate ecce enim merces vestra multa est in celo . In omnem .
paratext: explicit: 21r [D]eus qui beatum matheam apostolorum tuorum collegio sociasti tribue quesumus ut eius interuentione tue circa nos pietatis semper viscera lentiamur . Per Christum .
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 22r Georgi martir inclite te decet laus et gloria predotatum milicia per quem puella regia existent in tristicia coram dracone pessimo te rogans corde intimo saluata est et animo se reddidit altissimo cum multi fidelibus fac ergo sic ut ciuibus tu nos iungas celestibus nostris ablutis sordibus ut simul cum leticia tecum sumus in gloria nostraque reddant labia laudes Christo cum gratia .
paratext: explicit: 22v Omnipotens sempiterne deus qui deprecantium uoces benigne exaudis maiestatem tuam supplices exoramus ut sicut in honore beati et gloriosi martiris tui georgij draconem a puella superari voluisti isti ita eiusdem intercessione hostes nostros uisibiles et inuisiblies ne nocere nobis valeant concedere digneris . Per Christum dominum nostrum . Amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 22r Memoria de sancto georgionam

paratext: incipit: 22v [M]athee sancte bine pollens mun[ire] sedulis ihesum inter pella questibus vt nos in mundi gubernet turbinibus ne post eternus absorbiat interitus In omnem terram exiuit sonus etcaetera
paratext: explicit: 22v da nobis quesumus omnipotens deus vt beati apostoli tui mathei et Euangeliste veneranda solempnitas et deuotionem nobis augiat et salutem Per Christum dominum nostrum
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

work: title: Suffrage to St Simon and St Jude
paratext: incipit: 23r [B]eate symon et thadee inclite cernite nostas [sic] gemitus cum fletibus quique per lapsum meruimus baratrum per vos celorum meruimur aditum Annunciauerunt opera dei et facta eius intellexerunt
paratext: explicit: 23r Oremus - [D]eus qui nos per beatos apostolos tuos symonem et iudam ad agnissionem tui nominis venire tribuisti da nobis eorum gloriam sempiternam et proficiendo celeberare et ciliberando proficere Per Christum dominum nostrum. Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 24r Sancte Christofore martir ihesu Christe qui pro eius nomine penas pertulisti opem confer miseris atque mundo tristi qui celestis gloria regna meruisti Christofori sancti speciam quicumque tuertur illo nempe die nullo languore tenetur martir Christofore pro saluatoris honore fac nos mente fore dignos deitatis amore promisso Christi quiaque petis obtinuisti da populo tristi bonaque moriendo petisti confer solamen et mentis tolle grauamen iudicis examen fac mite sit omnibus amen
paratext: explicit: 24v Concede quesumus omnipotens et misericors deus ut qui beati Christofori martiris tui memoriam agimus eius pijs meritis et intercessionibus a morte subitanea peste fame timore pauperitate et ab omnibus insidijs inimicorum nostrorum liberemur in terris per te ihesu Christe saluator mundi quem Christoforus meruit in humeris suis portare . Qui viuis et regnas deus per omnia secula seculorum . Amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 24r Memoria de sancto Christofero

work: title: Suffrage to St Hugh of Lincoln [Avalon]
paratext: incipit: 24v Confessor domini Hugo Astantem plebem corrobora sancta intercessione vt qui victiorum pondee premimor beatitudinis tue gloria subleuemur et te duce eterna premia consequamur Amauit eum dominus et ornauit eum stola gloria induit eum
paratext: explicit: 24v-25r Oracio - Deus qui beatum hugonem confessorem atque pontificem eminentia meritorum et claritate signorum eccelenter ornasti concede propicius vt eius exempla nos provocent et virtutes illustrent . Per Christum dominum nostrum Amen . Pater noster .
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 26r Gaude felix anna que concepisti prolemque erat paritura Christum saluatorem
paratext: explicit: 26r-26v Domine ihesu Christe qui beate anne tantam gratiam donare dignatus es ut uirginem maria matrem tuam in vtero suo portare mereretur da quesumus ut per intercessionem matris ac dilectissime filie marie matris tue ut per illam sacratissimam intercessionem ab omni periculo corporis et anime nos defendas et presentis uite salutem conferas et ad lucem celestis gaudij perducat . Per Christum .
paratext: rubric(s): 26r Memoria de sancta anna matris marie

paratext: incipit: 26v [O] cuthberte quam aperte fulgit tua gracia nobis ferte nam nos parte speramus subsidia Tu de ferte pestem verte mortis a familia Vt nos parte vite certe senciamus gaudia . Ora pro nobis beate cuthberte Ut digni etcaetera
paratext: explicit: 26v-27r Oracio - Deus qui graciam tuam beate cuthberti confessoris tui atque pontificis mirabiliter revellare dignatus es da quesumus vt omnes eius sibi deuoti meritis intercessionibus a pestilencia a morte subitania et ab omni malo misericorditer liberenter per Christum dominum nostrum Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 28r Gaude uirgo katherina qua doctoris lex diuina traxit ab erroribus
paratext: explicit: 28r-28v Deus qui dedisti legem moysi in summitate montis synai et in eodem loco per sanctos angelos corpus beate katherine uirginis et martiris tue mirabiliter collocasti presta quesumus ut eius meritis et intercessione ad montem qui Christus est ualeamus peruenire Per Christum dominum nostrum .
paratext: rubric(s): 28r Memoria de sancta katherina

work: title: Suffrage to St James the Great
paratext: incipit: 29r [O] lux et decus hyspanie sanctissime iacobe apostole qui inter apostolos primatum tenes primus eorum martirio laureatus
paratext: explicit: 29r [P]rotector in te sperancium deus familiam tuam propicius iacobum a cunctis earum aduersitatibus potentie tue brachio defende Per Christum dominum nostrum . Amen .
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 30r Gaude pia magdalena spes salutis uite uena lapsorum fiducia
paratext: explicit: 30v Gaude qui beata marie magdalene penitenciam ita tibi placitam gratamque fecisti ut non solum peccata dimitteres ueram eciam singulari tui amoris gratia illius intima perlustrares da nobis quesumus ita digne flere mala que commisimus ut et sanctam indulgentiam consequi ualeamus et in omnibus petitionibus propiciationis tue clemenciam senciamus . Per Christum .
paratext: rubric(s): 30r Memoria de sancta maria magdalena

work: title: Suffrage to St James the Less
paratext: incipit: 31r [O] candor perpetue pure castitatis bona operarie doctor veritatis
paratext: explicit: 31r [D]eus qui iustum apostolum tuum iacobum perpetue castitatis flore candidatum ecclesie tue primum episcopum et tui operis vicarium preesse voluisti: concede quesumus vt ita ipse aperte sit pro nobis perpetuus intecessor: sicut tui mysterij extitit primus executor et doctor . Per Christum nostrum Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand. This suffrage is also found in a book of hours printed by Wynkyn de Worde in 1494 (see Edgar Hoskins, Horae Mariae Virginis or Sarum and York Primers with Kindred Books and Primers of the Reformed Roman Use (London: Longmans and Green, 1901), p. 113).
bibliography: bibl: Edgar Hoskins, Horae Mariae Virginis or Sarum and York Primers with Kindred Books and Primers of the Reformed Roman Use (London: Longmans and Green, 1901)

paratext: incipit: 32r Gaude barbara regina summa pollens in doctrina angeli misterio
paratext: explicit: 32r-32v Omnipotens sempiterne deus trina et vna inseperabilisque maiestas qui sanctissimam uirginem et martirem tuam barbaram in plena tui agnitione super ceteras illustrare dignetas es pretende ineffabilem misericordiam tuam nobis et largire ita deuotum eidem exhibere famulatatum ut diuinas gracias suscipiamus quas omnibus ipsam colentibus a te promeruit specialiter impetrare . Per Christum dominum nostrum .
paratext: rubric(s): 32r Memoria de sancta barbara veirgina

work: title: Suffrage to St Armagil of Brittany
paratext: incipit: 32v Sancte dei preciose . aduocate gloriose confessor Armagile
paratext: explicit: 33r Deus qui beatum Armigilum confessorem tuum mirabilibus et in muneris decorasti miraculis concede propicius : vt nos ab omni adversitate mentis et corporis semper liberemur supplicacionem que nostram ac audicionem votiuam consequi meriamur et feliciter ad eterne beatitudinis consorcium eius precibus perducamur Per Christum dominum nostrum Amen
bibliography: note(s): Added by a 15th-century hand.

paratext: incipit: 34r Gaude uirgo margareta que nutrices gregem letaminabas ad pascua
paratext: explicit: 34r-34v Deprecationem nostram quesumus domine benignus intende precesque nostras clementer exaudi atque misericordiam tuam nobis largire ut intercessione beate margarete uirginis tue exquacunque necessitate ad te clamauerimus almiflua consolationis tue beneficia consequamur . Per Christum .
paratext: rubric(s): 34r Memoria de sancta margarita uirgina

work: title: The Hours of the Virgin with memoriae at Lauds
paratext: incipit: 36r Domine labia mea aperies . Et os meum annunciabit laudem tuam .
paratext: explicit: 71r Omnipotens sempiterne deus qui gloriose uirginis et matris marie corpus et animam ut dignum filij tui habitaculum effici mereretur spiritu sancto cooperante mirabiliter preparasti da ut cuius commemoratione lecamur eius pia intercessione ab instantibus malis et a morte perpetua liberemur . Per Christum dominum nostrum . Amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 36r Incipiunt hore beate marie uirginis

work: title: The hymn Ave virgo virginum stella matutina (in the form of an exposition on the Salve regina)
paratext: incipit: 71r Salue uirgo uirginum stella matutina . Sordidorum criminum uera medicina Consolatrix hominum qui sunt in ruina . Precibus precancium mater te inclina .
paratext: explicit: 74v Deus qui de beate marie uirginis utero uerbum tuum angelo nunciante carnem suscipere uoluisti . Presta supplicibus tuis ut qui uere eam dei genitricem credimus eius apud te intercessionibus adiuuemur . Per Christum dominum nostrum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): 71r Has uideas laudes . Qui es sacra uirgine gaudes . Et uenerando piam . Studeas laudare mariam . uirginis intacte . cum veneris ante figuram . Pretereundo caue ne taceatur aue . Inuenies veniam sit salutando mariam . Salue

paratext: incipit: 75r O Intemerata et in eternum benedicta singularis atque in comparabilis uirgo dei genitrix maria gratissimum dei templum spiritus sancti
paratext: explicit: 77r Qui cum patre et filio coeternus et consubstancialis cum eis et in eis viuit et regnat omnipotens deus
paratext: rubric(s): 74v Ad beatam uirginem mariam .

paratext: incipit: 75r Obsecro te domina sancta maria mater dei pietate plenissima summi regis
paratext: explicit: 78r Et exaudi me dulcissima maria mater dei et misericordie Amen .

work: title: The Seven Joys of the Virgin Mary (with indulgence)
paratext: incipit: 78r Uirgo templum trinitatis deus summe bonitatis et misericordie
paratext: explicit: 79v O maria tota munda a peccatis nos emunda per hec septem gaudia . Et nos fecunda . et duc tecum ad iocunda paradysi gloria . Amen . Oratio.
paratext: rubric(s): 78r Quicumque heb septem gaudia in honre beate marie uirginis semel in die dixerit .C. dies indulgenciarum obtinebit a domino papa clemente qui hec septem gaudia proprio stilo composuit.

work: title: Salutations to the wounds of the Crown of Thorns and the Five Wounds
paratext: incipit: 80r cruentatum exemplar humilium . O corona preciosa quam cruoris tinxit rosa plasmatoris omnium . per te fiat speciosa mens humana mens spinosa declinans in uicium .
paratext: explicit: 80v Ad vulnus sinistri pedis . Veni pedis perforati aui vulnus in quo pati deus homo voluit . Comparandum es
bibliography: note(s): The sequence of prayers is imperfect both at the beginning and end.

paratext: incipit: 81r De precor sanctissima maria mater dei pietate plenissima summi regis filia mater gloriosissima mater
paratext: explicit: 81r Et post mortem cum sanctis et eelectis suis uitam eternam ac omnibus fidelibus viuis et defunctis uitam et requiem sempiternam . Amen.

work: title: Prayer to Christ on the Cross
paratext: incipit: 81v Omnibus consideratis paradysus uoluptatis es ihesu pijssime . in te fons paternitatis omnis fructus suauitatis plantauit plenissime . passionis tue fructus et cruoris tui fluctus defluens largissime finem fecit nostri luctus per hunc infernus destructus gemit amarissime
paratext: rubric(s): 81r Ad ymaginem Christi crucifixi .
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

paratext: incipit: 81v Triumphale lignum crucis tu seductos nos reducis ad superna gaudia portas pandis uere lucis fauces claudis hostis crucis . diuina potencia . es adoro propter illum qui per te gregem pusillum reduxit in patria . confringens per hoc vexillum orthi uectes et sigillum signans infernalia .
paratext: rubric(s): 81v Ad Crucem Christi
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

work: title: Prayer to the Wounded Head of Christ
paratext: incipit: Ave caput inclinatum despectiue coronatum spinis infidelium multis locis perforatum circumquaque cruentatum per te sumus liberati nos quos vmbra tenuit Dulce vulnus dulcis clauus et cruoris dulcis fauus per istud efferbuit Per te regat ignanus . emendetur homo prauus . in te qui spem habuit .
paratext: rubric(s): 81v Ad capud Christi
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

work: title: Prayer to St John the Evangelist
paratext: incipit: 82v Iohannes euuangelista tu sacram sacrista in quo deus iacuit . Me mundus fallit sophista per te michi dentur ista que supra meus uoluit Obsecro te per hunc flectum per dolorem et per metum quo cor tuum tremuit. Dum uideres deum spretum ut me ducas adhuc tecum quem Christus eripuit . Amen . Versus . Christus factus est pro nobis obediens usque ad mortem . mortem autem crucis . Versus Ora pro nobis sancta dei genitur . Ut digni efficiamur promissione Christi . Versus . Valde honorandus est beatus Iohannes euuangelista . qui supra pectus domini in cena recubuit . Domine exaudi . Oremus .
paratext: rubric(s): 82r Ad sanctam iohannem ewangelistam
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

work: title: Prayer to God invoking the Passion
paratext: incipit: 82v Omnipotens sempiterne deus qui vnigenitum filium tuum dominum nostrum ihesum Christum crucem coronam spineam et quinque vulnera subire uoluisti ut inimici a nobis expelleres potestatem qui et in cruce pendens mariam matrem suam uirginem uirgini commendauit presta quesumus ut omnes qui eius passionem ueneramur a peccatorum nostrorum nexibus eorum precibus liberemur . Per Christum
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

work: title: Prayer invoking the Seven Last Words of Christ on the Cross
paratext: incipit: 83r Domine ihesu Christe qui septem uerba die ultimo uite tue in cruce pendens dixisti ut semper illa sacratissima uerba in memoria habere mus
paratext: explicit: 84r Quod significat labores et dolores quos pro nobis miseris suscepisti iam fuisti fac ut audire merear illam dulcissimam vocem tuam dicentem michi veni amica mea quia iam disposui peticiones tuas consummari veni merum ut sedeas cum angelis meis sanctis in rengo meo epulari iocundari et commorari per in finita secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): 82v-83r Oratio uenerabilis bede presbiteri de septem verbis Christi in cruce pendentis quam creatorem quicunque cotidie deuote dixerit flexis genubus nec dyabolus nec malus homo ei nocere pote nec sine confessione morietur et per tringinta dies aute obitum suum uidebit gloriosam uirginem mariam in auxilium sibi preparatam .

paratext: incipit: 84r Precor te pijssime domine Ihesu Christe propter illam caritatem qua tu rex celestis pendebas in cruce cum deifica caritate
paratext: explicit: 84v ut sis michi placabilis super multitudinem peccatorum meorum faciam ultimo uite mee bonum et sanctum finem nec non gloriosam beatamque resurrectionem propter tuam misericordiam michi tribuere digneris . Amen .

paratext: incipit: 84v Ave domine ihesu Christe uerbum patris filius uirginis agnus dei salus mundi hostia sacra uerbum caro fons pietatis .
paratext: explicit: 85r Aue uerum corpus domini nostri ihesu Christi natum de maria uirgine uere passum immolatum in cruce pro homine Cuius latus perforatum uero fluxit sanguine esto nobis pregustatum mortis in examine . O dulcis O piet . O ihesu fili marie . miserere nostri . Amen .

paratext: incipit: 85r Ave caro Christi cara immolata crucis ara pro redemptis hostia . morte tua nos amara fac redemptos luce clara tecum frui gloria Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): 85r Oratio .
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

paratext: incipit: 85r-85v Anima Christi sanctifica me. corpus Christi salua me sanguis Christi inebria aqua lateris Christi laua me passio Christi conforta me mors Christi viuifica me O bone ihesu exaudi me ne permittas me seperari a te ab hoste maligno defende me in hora mortis uoca me et pone me iuxta te ut cum angelis laudem te in secula seculorum . amen .
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

paratext: incipit: 85v Domine ihesu Christe qui hanc sacratissimam carnem et preciosissimum sanguinem tuum de gloriose uirginis marie utero assumpsisti et eundem sanguinem de sacratissimo latere tuo in ara crucis pro salute nostra effudisti et in hac gloriosa carne a mortuis resurrexisti . et ad celos ascendisti et iterum venturus es iudicare viuos et mortuos in eadem carne libera me per hoc sacrosanctum corpus tuum quod modo tractatur in altari in omnibus in mundicijs mentis et corporis et ab vniuersis malis periculis presentibus preteritis et futuris . amen .
paratext: rubric(s): 85v Omnibus confessis et conteritus hanc oracionem dicentibus inter eleuacionem corpus Christi et tercium agnus dei dominus papa bonifacius concessit duo milia annorum indulgenciarum ad supplantationem philippi regis francie
bibliography: note(s): Full transcription.

paratext: incipit: 87r Antiphona . Ne reminiscaris . Psalmus . Domine ne in furore tuo arguas me neque in ira tua corupias me.
paratext: explicit: 92r Et perdes omnes qui tribulant animam meam quam ego seruus tuus sum. Gloria patri. Antiphona Ne reminiscaris domine delicta nostra uel parentum meorum neque vindictam sumas de peccatis nostris. Antiphona. Parce domine

bibliography: note(s): Tables for finding the position of the sun in: A bissextile year One year after a bissextile year Two years after a bissextile year Three years after a bissextile year A bissextile year is a leap year. In the modern Gregorian calendar we add a leap day on the 29th March, but the practice of adding a leap day every four years (with minor adjustments) significantly predates the adoption of the Gregorian calendar in western Europe. The Romans also adjusted their calendars to the length of the solar year by adding an extra day to February every four years, but they did it by doubling the 24th of February, which was better-known in their calendar as the 6th day before the kalends of March (ante diem sextum Kalendas), causing a doubled 6th day (before the kalends of March) i.e., a bis+sextile day.

The calendar contains copious contemporary and later additions. Mnemonic for the progression of ferial letters for the first day of each month written in red in the lower margin of each page of the calendar: A | dam | de | ge | bat | er | go | ci | fos | a | dri | fex (i.e., ADDGBEGCFADF) Mneomnic poem for the dies aegyptiaci ('Egyptian days'), each line of the poem contains two numbers, the first of which should be counted (inclusively) from the beginning of the month to find the first 'Egyptian day', and the second of which should be counted backward from the end of the month to find the second. For example, the first number in the January verse is 1 (prima) and the first day counted inclusively from the first day of January is 1 January. The second number in the January verse is seven (septima) and the seventh day counted inclusively from the end of January (i.e., 31 Jan) is the 25th of January, making the 'Egyptian days' for January the 1st and 25th of the month. The text on the leaves is as follows: Page 1: Decretum III 26.14-15 Page 1: Decretum III 26.14-15 In March 2024, Dr James Freeman observed that pp. 1-8 in Cambridge, Gonville and Caius, MS 181/214 derive from the same manuscript source as Gonville and Caius College, MS 178/211, ff. [i]-[iv]; in both cases four leaves from a legal manuscript have been inserted sideways and used as flyleaves at the beginning of a volume of medical texts. Both Gonville and Caius MS 178/211 and MS 181/214 were owned by Roger Marchall Roger Marchall , and both sets of flyleaves were used by him to record his name and a list of the contents of the respective volumes on the last page (i.e., Gonville and Caius MS 181/214, p. 8 and Gonville and Caius MS 178/211, f. [iv] verso) of that group of endleaves. Both volumes have been rebound since Marchall's death in 1477, but it is plausible that each binding may have resembled the other's in Marchall's lifetime as the shared source of endleaves, both with Marchall annotations, suggest that they were both bound by the same workshop on Marchall's behalf.

bibliography: note(s): Page 42, full transcription: Est quedam aqua nobilis pro omni vicio oculorum que quidem aqua . Dominus Rex Edwardus pater utebatur per consilium magistri Nicholai de Tyngewyco et aliorum medicorum peritissimorum . R . T . herbarum feniculi rute eufrasie . veruene . Tormentille betonice rubre rostri porcinisowethistil gallatriciioculus christi ipiechekynmete pimpernelle rubre donie pionie filaginis foliorum vitis apii ... nie caprifolijwodebynde . ana . prima die trite ponantur in albo secunda die in urina pueri masculi et virginis tercia die in lacte mulieris Quarta die in bono . et tunc postea distillentur in aqua. Hinc custodiatur in vase vitreo quia est aquarum nobilissima pro omni causa According to Feltoe and Minns this text may have been copied by Scribe F1. Another version of this recipe in  Cambridge, St John's College, MS E.6, 'Thomas Betson's Notebook', f. 107r, ln. 9 seq . The Cambridge, St John's College, MS E.6 version of the recipe is transcribed in J. Adams, and S. Forbes (eds.), The Syon Abbey Herbal: The Last Monastic Herbal in England, c. AD 1517: From St. John’s College, Cambridge Manuscript 109 (E.6) (London: AMCD, 2015), p. 279. Adams and Forbes read the initial of the medical practitioner's name in the St John's College MS as a 'W' and expanded the name as 'Willelmi', but the initial in Cambridge, St John's College MS E.6 is 'N' and should be expanded to 'Nicholai, in agreement with the name in Gonville and Caius MS 204/110. A Nicholas de Tyngewick (Tingewick) was a royal physician to King Edward I abd provided significant treatment when the king was taken ill at Lanercost Priory in 1306; Tyngewick was later associated with the royal court of King Edward II - see C. H. Talbot, and E. A. Hammond, The Medical Practitioners in Medieval England : A Biographical Register (London: Wellcome Historical Medical Library, 1965). Similar recipe in  Cambridge, University Library, MS Dd.8.12, f. i (front pastedown)

work: title: Poem in Latin with Middle English glosses
bibliography: note(s): Short verse, possibly from the Gesta romanorum, in a late medieval hand on f. 267v: Spexus ovem geminam per spinam traxit equinam Lesus surgit . equs pondum utrumque pecus Ad molendinum pondus portabat ouinum Dispergendo focum se cremat atque locum. The poem is very similar to one found in the Gesta romanorum ch. 163 (Oesterley, 1872 edition), and appears by itself in a few other medieval manuscripts (see WIC 11754). The version of the poem in Cambridge, Jesus College, MS Q.D.4 lacks the final line Custodes aberant . singula dampna ferant. It should perhaps be noted that an inscription on f. 269v states that this volume (Q.D.4) was part of a trade by a John Thrope in exchange for a copy of the Gesta romanorum.

bibliography: note(s): The collection mostly concerns medical recipes but ends with different types of recipes, including: Magical recipes (p. 102), including methods to obtain a woman's secrets by placing an amber or jet stone on her body during sleep and to prevent a goose's chickens from dying by giving them water to drink in which bread or parchment inscribed with the Lord's Prayer has been washed. Gynaecological recipes (pp. 103-104), including methods to help a couple become pregnant, a method for establishing whether the cause for unwanted childlessness in a couple lies with the man or the woman, and methods for establishing the sex of an unborn child. Cosmetic recipes (pp. 103-104), including methods to dye hair black and blond ('gold') and remove blemishes. Repellants (pp. 102-103, 105), including methods to stop dogs from barking at you, drive flies out of a house, and keep wolves from a piece of land. Household/Practical recipes (pp. 105-106), including methods to open a silver ring by adding mercury to it and join to pieces of meat together. Equestrian medicine (p. 105-106), including recipes for healing ailments in horses. Horticultural instructions (p. 107), including methods for harvesting grapes and cherries all year round. ; McKitterick and Beadle (1992), p. 3, point out that many of the recipes on pp. 59-107 also appear in a collection of recipes in Lincoln, Cathedral Library, MS 91 [The Lincoln Thornton Manuscript], entitled 'Liber de diversis medicinis' but this is not the case for most of the specified non-medical recipes.; The collection contains a previously unidentified selection of recipes from John Arderne's Treatises of fistula in ano : haemorrhoids, and clysters: 'Sanguis veneris' (pp. 156-157; 'Valens of Scabius' (pp. 158-159); 'Valence of Wourmot' (pp. 159-160).

bibliography: note(s): This is a previously unidentified copy of The Alchemical Waters of Saint Giles. For an edition of this work from other manuscripts, see Willy L. Braekman, 'The Alchemical Waters of Saint Giles: Text and Context', in Studies on Alchemy, Diet, Medecine and Prognostication in Middle English, Scripta: Mediaeval and Renaissance Texts and Studies, 22 (Brussels: Omirel, 1986), pp. 7-41. Braekman identifies Latin and vernacular versions of the work, including three English copies: 1. Cambridge, Trinity College, MS R.14.32, ff. 96r-98v; 2. London, British Library, Harley MS 2381, ff. 56v-60r; 3. London, British Library, Sloane MS 706, ff. 128v-132r. A similar work, not identified by Braekman, is extant in Cardiff, National Library of Wales, Peniarth 369, ff. 36r-38r entitled: Here bygynnyth doctor Gylys þe boke of vertuse and of wateres þat he made in deserte by þe which all sekenes curyd þat wer curabull. The connnection between St Giles and the nine waters is unclear, but Braekman suggests that the work may have been attributed to him because of cures that are described in his vita or because he, as the patron saint of blacksmiths, was associated with the furnace and the latter was also employed by alchemists (see Braekman (1986), p. 20). Additionally, the fact that this saint, according to his vita, lived near the mouth of the Rhône and the River Gard in Septimania, may have associated him with healing waters.

The recipe has the heading 'Preseruatiua regis Edwardi iiiite'. The scribe of the recipe has been identified as Thomas Deynman (fl. c. 1473, d. 1501), Bachelor of Medicine and Master of Peterhouse Deynman, Thomas, fl. c. 1473, d. 1501 by R. M. Thomson, and Roger Marchall (c. 1417-1477) Rogerus Marshall -1477 by Linda Voigts. Marchall was physician to Edward IV, and Deynman to Henry VII, but the hand of the recipe appears more like Deynman's than Marchall's; Marchall and Deynman knew each other, presumably through their Peterhouse connection and subsequent roles as royal physicians, and Deynman seems to have had access to several of Marchall's manuscripts (including this one) after Marchall's death in 1477, so it is not impossible for Deynman to have copied one of Marchall's recipes for Edward IV into one of Marchall's manuscripts.

work: title: Collection of medical recipes and charms
language: text lang(s): Middle English recipes and Latin and Middle English charms with headers in Latin or Middle English
paratext: incipit: 1:1r er drynke þe poudyr of a bak er sonp it with a nesche ey
paratext: explicit: 1:29r pocio pro wlnere: Stampe mader in red cole lues and leues of hemp and tenze be euen with and sethe þes thinges in quit wine or in water and ley on þe wonde and red cole lef
bibliography: note(s): The collection contains a wide variety of recipes, including recipes informed by popular beliefs. For example, a recipe for healing sore eyes (ff. 1:6r-1:6v) uses powder made from a swallow's chick and the gall of a puppy. The recipe instructs one to first prick out the eyes of the swallow's chick with a needle and then return to the next after nine days to find the chick again with restored eyesight. This practice is based on the belief that swallows had a magical stone with which they could heal their young. The recipe reads as follows: Take þe a swalwis brid out þe nest and tak a nedle and prikykyt [sic] in þe eyne til it is blind sithe put aȝen þat brid into þe nest and aftir ix dayes þou schal fynde þat bride wel seande tak þat brid and puttit with al þe fetheris into a clene newe erthene potte and bren it al to pouder take þan þe galle of a sokande qwelpe þat hath sokyd xxx dayes and tak two partes of þe pouder of castor and mdle al þis to gidere and putyt in a sorre eye. ; The collection also contains various charms: An instruction for making a birthing girdle from cloth and parchment onto which is written a charm to help a pregnant woman deliver a child: To don a wiman be deliuered of a child (ff. 1:7v-1:8r) [crossed out]. Saint William's charm for gout and other ailments: Þis is þe charm of seynt William þat angel gabriel brout him fro oure lord to j armen cristene men for worm and vein and goute and rancle and sor first do singyn a messe in hnour sancti spiritus et tunc dic istud carmen (ff. 1:23r-1:23v). A charm for healing wounds that involves a led plate with five crossed on it: A charm to holen a wonde with a plate of led (ff. 1:23v-1:24r). A charm agains fevers: ffor þe feueris Oracio bona (ff. 1:27r-1:27v) [the charm invokes King Edmund the martyr]. A charm against fevers: Contra febres + [the charm invokes 'seven sisters’ ('septem sorores') fever demons who are named after seven types of fever] (ff. 1:27v-1:28r). A charm for healing a wound or sore: A charm for a wonde and for a sorre (f. 1:28r). ; The collection also contains recipes that are not strictly aimed at healing: Methods to control animals, including one to to prevent birds from nesting in trees: To kacchen briddis fro here nisterlynge (ff. 1:6v-1:7r and another one to drive flies away: ffor to don a wey flies (f. 1:8r). paratext: explicit: f. 70r προσθῶμεν ἐλεημοσύνην καὶ προσευχὴν. ἵνα τύχωμεν τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος ὥσπερ καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος· καὶ δοξάσωμεν Πατέρα Υἱὸν καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα· αὐτῶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοῦς αἰῶνας ἀμήν

work: title: Quod grave sit Dei clementiam contemnere
paratext: incipit: f. 70v Ἡ μὲν τῆς δεσποτικῆς φιλανθρωπίας ἀρτίως ἀκούομεν ἡ φιλοτιμία πολλῆς καὶ μυρίων ἁμαρτίας
paratext: explicit: f. 70v οὐ γὰρ εὑρίσκεται τρόπος τῆς αὐτῶν διορθώσεως
paratext: rubric(s): f. 70v Τοῦ αὐτοῦ ὅτι βαρυ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ φιλανθρωπίας καταφρονεῖν· ἐρρέθη δε τῆς τῶν μυρίων ταλάντων ἀναγνωσθείσης παραβολῆς καὶ κατὰ Ἰουδαίων τοῦ σεισμοῦ γενομένου
bibliography: note(s): Attributed to Chrysostom.; PG 64, 17-18; CPG 4697; Aldama 156; TLG 2062.355

paratext: incipit: f. 71r Οὐκ οἶδα τί χρήσομαι λόγοις σήμερον· καὶ γὰρ ὁρῶν τὰς συνάξεις ἐλαττουμένας· προφήτας ὑβριζομένους
paratext: explicit: f. 80v βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐπιτύχωμεν· ἧς γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἐπιτυχεῖν· χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπία τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· δι’ οὗ καὶ μεθ’ οὗ τῶ Πατρὶ ἡ δόξα· ἅμα τῶ ἁγίω Πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ἀμήν
paratext: rubric(s): f. 71r Τοῦ αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς τὰς συνάξεις καταλειμπάνοντας· καὶ ἔτι οὐ μόνον χρησιμωτέρον τοῖς ἐν θεάτροις διαγωγῆς ἡ ἐν ἐκκλησία διατριβὴ. Ἀλλὰ καὶ ἴδιον· καὶ εἰς τὴν δευτέραν ῥησιν τῆς εὐχῆς τῆς Ἄννας· καὶ εἰς τὸ δεῖν συνεχως εὔχεσθαι καὶ ἐν παντὶ τόπω· κἂν ἐν ἀγορὰ ὤμεν· κἂν ἐν ὁδῶ κὰν ἐπικλινης

work: title: In illud: Ne timueritis cum dives factus fuerit homo, homilia 1
paratext: incipit: f. 80v Ὁ μὲν γηπόνος τὸ ἄροτρον εἰς καθαρισμὸν ἔλκει τῆς ἀροῦρας. καὶ τὴν αὔλακα ἀνατεμεῖν
paratext: explicit: f. 92r τοῦτον λαβόντες τὸν στίχον. ἐξάρξωμεν τὸν στίχον τοῦτον τῆς βακτηρίας· ὑπὲρ δὴ τούτων ἁπάντων. εὐχαριστήσωμεν τῶ Πατρὶ καὶ τῶ Υἱῶ καὶ τῶ ἁγίω Πνεύματι· ὅτι αὐτῶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν
paratext: rubric(s): f. 80v Τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγος εἰς τὸ ῥητὸν τοῦ προφήτου τὸ λέγον· μὴ φοβοῦ ὅταν πλουτήσει ἄνθρωπος καὶ περὶ φιλοξενίας

paratext: incipit: f. 92r Αἱ τῶν μαρτύρων ἑορταὶ· οὐκ ἐν τῆ περιόδω τῶν ἡμερῶν μόνον. ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆ γνώμη τῶν ἐπιτελούντων κρίνονται
paratext: explicit: f. 93v ἀλλὰ βούλη τρυφᾶν. περίμενε τῶ τάφω τοῦ μάρ

paratext: incipit: f. 100v Πρὸς τὸ τέλος ἡμῖν τῆς νηστείας λοιπὸν ὁ καιρὸς ἐπήγεται· οὐκ’ οὖν καὶ ἡμεῖς πρὸς πλείονα ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιδῶμεν ἀρετήν
paratext: explicit: f. 115v πάντα διορθώσαντες ἐλαττώματα, τυχεῖν τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν· χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπία τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· μεθ’ οῦ τῶ Πατρὶ σὺν ἁγίω Πνεύματι· δόξα τιμὴ καὶ προσκύνησις· νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν
paratext: rubric(s): f. 100v Τοῦ αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὐκ ἀρκῆ ἡ νηστεία Τεσσαρακοστης· πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι κοινωνεῖν· ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς κατα ψυχὴν ἀρετῆς πρώτης· καὶ πῶς δυνατὸν μὴ μνησικακεῖν· καὶ ὅτι πολὺς τῶ Θεῶ τοῦ νόμου τούτου λόγος· καὶ ὅτι πρὸ τῆς γεέννης τὸ μνησηκακεῖν κολάζει τοὺς αλόντας
